catalog_quote: Stress is usually not indicated, since it regularly falls on the penultimate syllable in all Tomini-Tolitoli languages. Only the exceptions to this rule are marked. Primary stress is marked by an acute accent <´>, secondary stress (i.e. lengthening of reduplicated syllables) by a grave accent . Most exceptions to the general stress rule are well-motivated (either a phonetically long vowel is shortened (cf. §3.4.6 above) or stress moves to the first member of a sequence of unlike vowels as in táipang 'mango', which occurs as an alternate to the regular taípang). In Balaesang, however, stress also occurs on final short closed syllables as in moontol [montól] 'sharp'. This includes syllables which are closed by a non-phonemic glottal stop, e.g. ita pronounced as [itá'] 'we (exclusive)'.

Also confirmed: printed pp.91-92 (PDF 113-114) 'The difference between suffixes and clitics/free forms is evident in stress assignment. Suffixed forms receive regular penultimate stress, i.e. the suffixes.. cause the stres…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the phonological word in every Tomini-Tolitoli language in the sourcebook's sample, which includes both documented varieties of Taje (Petapa and Tanampedagi). Suffixes count toward the word so stress shifts rightward to stay penultimate; clitics and free forms do not shift it (p.92).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Secondary stress is defined only as the lengthening of a reduplicated syllable (accented (C)CV-reduplication, RDP1), marked with a grave accent; speakers vary in how strongly the reduplicated syllable is stressed (p.81).
new_statements.exceptions: Marked exceptions: a phonetically long vowel that is shortened (sec. 3.4.6); stress on the first member of a sequence of unlike vowels (táipang ~ taípang); paragogic vowels in the northern Tomini languages do not attract stress, giving surface antepenultimate stress (sec. 3.4.7; not reported for Taje); Balaesang alone stresses final short closed syllables; Lauje final-vowel deletion leaves stress on the now-final syllable. Petapa Taje adds a final vowel (usually /i/) to consonant-final bases (sec. 3.5.4, p.79) but the book does not say whether this vowel takes stress. The text layer strips accents, so Taje word-list entries carrying an irregular-stress mark were not extracted.
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word (base plus suffixes); statement is a group-level rule for all Tomini-Tolitoli languages in the sample, given in the phonological introduction to the word lists rather than in a Taje-specific paragraph; based on the compiler's own 1990s elicitation (contributors from Tanampedagi/Sidole and Petapa listed pp.xii-xiii), citation forms.
new_statements.identity_note: Himmelmann 2001 documents two Taje varieties, Petapa Taje (Dusun Kamonji, Petapa, Kecamatan Parigi) and Tanampedagi Taje (Sidole/Tanampedagi and Singura/Sipotara, Kecamatan Ampibabo); both fall under Glottolog taje1237 (alt name Petapa), which has no dialect-level glottocodes. The stress statement is a group-level rule covering all sampled Tomini-Tolitoli languages including both Taje varieties; Himmelmann 2001 treats Taje as Tomini-Tolitoli whereas Glottolog 5.x (Zobel 2020) files it under Greater Tomini > South Tomini.
